rationale: Two blocking findings. CR-001 (critical): the alias column in IntegrationsTab.tsx is declared type:'string'; TableCell only calls customRenderColumns when type===Custom, so the <span id> renderer never fires — contextId references a ghost element and aria-labelledby silently drops it, leaving the button with only 'More options' as its accessible name. The fix is structurally ineffective. CR-002 (major): the alias cell fallback uses literal '-' instead of credential_type, degrading accessible names for empty-alias rows ('More options -' vs the removed 'More options for jira'). No-spec round (confidence low due to no acceptance criteria; both findings are concrete correctness issues confirmed by edge-case lens with repo access).

standards_review.notes: Commit subject starts with EPMCDME-8420: ticket reference, imperative verb, under 72 chars.

findings.problem: alias column defined with type:'string' — TableCell only invokes customRenderColumns for type===Custom, so the <span id='user-setting-name-${item.id}'> renderer is never called. contextId on NavigationMore references a non-existent DOM element; aria-labelledby silently drops it; button accessible name is only 'More options' with no row context.
findings.impact: The entire accessibility improvement is ineffective. contextId approach does not work without the alias column being type Custom.
findings.recommendation: In IntegrationsTab.tsx getTableColumns(), change the alias column definition from type:'string' to type:Custom (DefinitionTypes.Custom or equivalent). Verify ProjectSettings does not unintentionally receive a customRenderColumns.alias that conflicts.

findings.problem: alias cell fallback is literal '-' for empty alias, producing accessible name 'More options -'. The removed accessibleName used item.credential_type as a fallback, giving a meaningful name like 'More options for jira'.
findings.impact: For integrations with no alias (common), the accessible name is less descriptive than before the fix.
findings.recommendation: Change alias renderer fallback: {item.alias || item.credential_type || 'Integration'} to match the removed accessibleName logic.
